# The product screen is its composition, and configuration happens after adding

**ID**: `cpt-gearbox-adr-product-composition`

## Table of Contents

<!-- generated by `cfs toc` -->

## Context and Problem Statement

Opening a product showed **Overview**, a summary of a resolution, and its gear list was built from
`resolution.product.gears`. Two consequences followed from that one choice.

A product whose resolution failed rendered as **visually empty**. The description was on disk and
perfectly readable, but the screen drew from the resolution, so nothing that could not be resolved
could be seen — which is exactly the state a person needs to look at the product in.

Configuring a gear meant leaving. The Catalogue held the gear, the Inspector held its config and
features, and the product screen held neither; so the answer to "what is in this product and how is
it set up" was spread across three surfaces, and the act of setting something up began by navigating
away from the thing being set up.

`cpt-gearbox-adr-create-product` built the surgical editor and the Create/Clone wizard, and
explicitly left `plugins = [...]` entry editing, per-plugin `config` and per-plugin `profiles` **out
of scope**. Plugin connections were therefore visible and not editable.

## Decision Outcome

**Chosen:** the product screen opens on a **Composition** stage built from the *intent*; gears and
their plugin connections are configured in place; adding is a modal catalogue dialog; and the
surgical editor gains per-entry plugin operations.

### The composition is built from the intent, not the resolution

`ProductIntent.selected_gears` is what the person wrote. It is available whenever the file parses,
which is a strictly weaker condition than resolving, so the composition survives a failed resolve.

The resolution is not discarded — it *annotates*. Computed dependencies appear in a separate
"Automatically included" group with their `selected_by` reasons; effective values and diagnostics
come from it. The division is: **the intent says what is there, the resolution says what follows.**

A gear stays visible when the catalogue has no descriptor for it. The saved id is shown with a
loading or unavailable note, because a product is not less real for the catalogue being slow.

### A resolution error does not take the screen

`landOnErrors` moved to Validation whenever the resolution carried errors. That was right while the
arriving stage was Overview — a summary says nothing about a product that did not resolve — and is
wrong now: the composition is there, and it is what was asked for.

The method is `stageForOpenProduct` and lands on Composition. Errors reach a person through the
count on the Validation tab and the summary line, both of which name the object. The trip is chosen.

Unreadable is different from unresolved: when no intent can be produced at all, the panel *is* a
recovery state with Retry and Open GDL, because there is no composition to fall back to.

### Settings are components, not a borrowed widget

The Composition pane and the Inspector render the same forms. They are components —
`GearSettings`, `PluginSettings` — taking their scratch state as local state, keyed on the draft
epoch so a Discard or an Apply remounts them.

The rejected alternative is worth recording because it was briefly built: the Product widget
injected `InspectorWidget` and called a public `renderContent()` on it. That made two surfaces one
widget instance with one set of half-typed new-key boxes, so typing a config key in the composition
pane changed what the right-hand panel showed.

### Adding is a dialog over the catalogue

A large modal with search, the candidate list, and what the addition would do — arriving gears,
applications, binding changes, new diagnostics, and the GDL diff — behind one **Add to product**
button. Detailed config and features are deliberately *not* here: they belong to the gear once it is
in the product, which is the whole shape of this ADR. See
`cpt-gearbox-adr-domain-specific-ide-shell` Amendment 2026-09-18 for what being a dialog costs.

### A plugin connection is addressed by where it is written

This is the part with a real trap in it.

GDL gives a `plugin(...)` call no identity. The same implementation may legitimately appear twice
under one host for disjoint profiles — that is what `profiles = [...]` is for — so neither the
plugin id nor the pair `(host, plugin)` distinguishes them. The address is the **position**:
`PluginTarget { gear, plugin, entry_index }`.

`entry_index` counts **written** entries, not evaluated ones, and is carried on
`PluginSelection.entry_index` rather than recomputed by the client. Evaluation drops an entry whose
id does not parse and an entry that duplicates a selection, so a client counting the selections it
received would address the wrong `plugin(...)` as soon as one malformed sibling existed — precisely
when the others most need editing.

That drift is currently unreachable: both skips also push an *error*, and `eval_product` yields no
intent when any error is present, so no client ever holds an intent with an entry missing. The field
exists because the editor's correctness should not rest on that coincidence, and
`an_unusable_plugin_entry_yields_no_intent_at_all` pins the coincidence so that relaxing it fails a
test rather than silently mis-aiming an edit.

`set_plugins` is **not** used for any of this. It rebuilds the list as bare `plugin("id")` entries
and its own documentation admits it drops profiles and per-plugin config from the entries it did not
mean to touch.

### One document snapshot per batch, and no rebasing

Staleness is `ApplyEditsParams.expected_before`: the text the client previewed, compared once for
the whole batch. An earlier design also stamped the full document onto every `PluginTarget`; that
was removed, because two guards over the same fact can disagree and it copied the document once per
target onto the wire.

A batch that removes an entry and also edits a later one under the same host is **refused**, not
rebased. The fold rewrites the text as it goes, so the removal moves what the later edit addresses;
rebasing would silently reinterpret what a person confirmed, and the preview they agreed to was
computed without it.

## Consequences

* A product with a resolution error is inspectable and editable, which it was not.
* Plugin connections are fully manageable: add with a scope, remove one entry, set one key, change
  one scope — each leaving every neighbouring entry, comment and profile setting untouched.
* The Inspector is a plain widget again, and the same forms serve both surfaces.
* Three `cpt-gearbox-adr-domain-specific-ide-shell` claims were re-pointed; see that ADR's
  Amendment 2026-09-18.
* Conformance claims that asserted config and features *inside* the add flow no longer describe it,
  and are re-pointed at the product.

## Confirmation

* `crates/gearbox-gdl/src/edit_tests.rs` — per-entry editing: siblings, other hosts, comments and
  profile scopes survive; two entries of one plugin addressed separately; a malformed sibling does
  not block editing the others; add-then-remove is an inverse; a stale position is refused.
* `crates/gearbox-rpc/src/apply_edits_tests.rs` — batch folding and the refusal above.
* `crates/gearbox-gdl/tests/product.rs` — `entry_index` is the written position, and the
  suppression rule that currently makes positions safe.
* `ide/tests/regression.spec.ts` — an error-carrying resolution arrives on, and stays on,
  Composition; the count is the way to the problem.

### Traceability

* Extends `cpt-gearbox-adr-create-product`, which left plugin-entry editing out of scope.
* Tier 3 of `cpt-gearbox-adr-authoring-ownership-tiers`: surgical edits, never re-serialisation.
* Amends `cpt-gearbox-adr-domain-specific-ide-shell` for the Add Gear surface.
